title: Financial System Capture
description: Central banking systems and payment networks have historically concentrated power in opaque institutions despite initially serving coordination functions
source: Historical analysis of central banking development

title: Social Platform Centralization
description: Platforms like Facebook and Twitter began as coordination tools but evolved into centralized control systems with opaque algorithmic governance

title: Cross-Cultural Trade Breakdown
description: International commerce requires extensive legal and institutional frameworks to substitute for absent social trust mechanisms

title: Game Theory Research
description: Experimental evidence shows cooperation rates decline significantly in anonymous, one-shot interactions compared to repeated games with identity

title: Prisoner's Dilemma Experiments
description: Laboratory studies showing that actors consistently defect in one-shot games even when mutual cooperation would yield better outcomes, demonstrating how structural incentives override individual preferences
source: Axelrod, R. (1984). The Evolution of Cooperation

title: Platform Capture Examples
description: Historical analysis of how Facebook, Twitter, and financial institutions initially promised decentralization but evolved toward centralized control through opaque algorithmic governance and network effects
source: Zuboff, S. (2019). The Age of Surveillance Capitalism

title: Cross-Border Trade Statistics
description: Economic data showing significantly higher transaction costs and lower cooperation rates in international compared to domestic trade, correlating with absence of shared reputation systems

title: Estonia's e-Residency Program
description: Case study of how digital identity infrastructure enabled new forms of cross-border business cooperation and reduced transaction costs for international entrepreneurs

title: Systematic failures on ARC dataset
description: Large language models show poor performance on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus, which tests novel pattern recognition and logical reasoning without relying on memorized knowledge
source: Chollet (2019) and subsequent LLM evaluations on ARC

title: Causal reasoning benchmark failures
description: Studies show LLMs struggle with counterfactual reasoning, causal identification, and distinguishing correlation from causation in scenarios not well-represented in training data
source: Kıcıman et al. (2023) on causal reasoning in LLMs

title: Transformer architecture analysis
description: The transformer architecture underlying LLMs performs next-token prediction based on attention patterns over training sequences, without explicit symbolic reasoning mechanisms
source: Vaswani et al. (2017) and architectural analyses

title: Adversarial prompt brittleness
description: LLMs show systematic failures when prompts are modified in ways that shouldn't affect reasoning but change statistical patterns, suggesting dependence on surface correlations
